justification: S3 increment 2 — inline contract-drift tripwire on REAL traffic. Railway CLI is not authed (a sampled cron can't be deployed/verified now), and the inline approach is strictly better: every production brief run now checks each typed service output (flood/bushfire/shadow) against its S2 contract and logs a loud CONTRACT-DRIFT warning the moment a contract key goes missing (a rename/drop -> the #589 silent-null class). Behaviour is unchanged — the card still fail-softs to None — but the drift becomes visible in prod logs on real traffic instead of only when a user notices a blank card. _warn_on_drift wraps check_drift (S3 #599) in try/except so drift-logging can never affect the brief, and lazily imports it (no circular import). Fully unit-tested via caplog. The proactive Telegram-alert cron remains a deploy-after-login follow-up.

pre_impl.existing_data: The typed builds (_build_flood_detail/_build_bushfire_detail/_build_shadow_result) parse via the S2 contracts; check_drift (scripts/brief_contract_drift.py) compares an output's keys to a contract. scripts/ is importable in the brief (it already imports conveyancing_db). check_drift does not import intelligence_brief (only _registry does, lazily).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: A cron sampling demo addresses needs Railway auth + the full image and misses inputs it doesn't sample; checking on real traffic in-process covers every real run with zero infra.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reused check_drift (#599); added a thin _warn_on_drift logger call at the top of each typed build. No behaviour change.
pre_impl.external_source_error: A drifted real output now logs CONTRACT-DRIFT with the exact missing key; the card still degrades to None as before.
pre_impl.frontend_type: Backend only. Full suite passes incl 2 new caplog tests.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: a service rename silently nulled a card and was only found by a user noticing a blank. After: every real brief run that hits the drifted service logs a loud CONTRACT-DRIFT warning naming the missing key.

functions.name: _warn_on_drift
functions.input: a Pydantic contract class, the raw service output, and a service label
functions.output: a CONTRACT-DRIFT warning log line naming the missing contract keys when the real output drifts; nothing on a clean output
functions.if_none: any exception in the check is swallowed so drift-logging can never affect the brief

values: N/A - logging only, not regulatory values.

break_it.scenario: The drift import or check raises at runtime
break_it.what_happens: it must never break the brief
break_it.how: the whole body is wrapped in try/except: pass; the brief proceeds regardless

break_it.scenario: A genuine all-None output (real nothing-detected) logs spurious drift
break_it.what_happens: noise in the logs on a normal run
break_it.repro: an output with all contract keys present but None
break_it.how: drift is key-presence not value; all-None with the right keys logs nothing. Guarded by test_build_flood_no_warning_on_good_output

break_it.scenario: A drifted output stops the card from building
break_it.what_happens: the brief should still build the card (fail-soft) and just log
break_it.how: the warning is logged then the existing tolerant parse runs; the card still builds. Guarded by test_build_flood_logs_drift_warning (asserts fd is not None)

post_merge.manual_verify: Run a brief; on a service whose output matches the contract there is no CONTRACT-DRIFT log. The proactive Telegram cron is a deploy-after-`railway login` follow-up.
